instruction:
Loose-geometry cleanup

The file `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\loose.dae` is a COLLADA scene exported from a SketchUp model that has **20 top-level `<node>` elements** under the visual scene root. Each top-level node holds a single small piece of geometry (either a short `<lines>` edge set or a tiny `<triangles>` face set), with its world coordinates baked into the vertices (no node transform is used).

Among the 20 top-level nodes:

1. **Exactly 10 are "connected"**: every one of them shares at least one vertex position (within a 0.1 mm tolerance) with the vertex of at least one OTHER top-level node, and together the 10 form a single connected component under the "shares a vertex" relation.
2. **Exactly 10 are "isolated"**: none of their vertex positions coincide (within 0.1 mm) with any vertex of any other top-level node.

Your task is to perform a two-part cleanup.

1. Parse `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\loose.dae` and, for every top-level `<node>`, extract its world-space vertex set.
2. Build the connectivity graph on those top-level nodes using a 0.1 mm vertex-coincidence tolerance. Treat two top-level nodes as adjacent iff at least one pair (one vertex from each) is within 0.1 mm.
3. A top-level node is **kept** iff it belongs to a connected component of size >= 2 (i.e. it shares at least one vertex with another top-level node). A top-level node is **deleted** iff it is a singleton (size-1 component).
4. Write `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\cleaned.dae`: a valid COLLADA file whose visual scene has **exactly one top-level `<node>` named `Leftovers`**, and whose direct children are the `<node>` entries you kept (reusing their original node names and geometry; no transform changes to the vertices). Deleted nodes must not appear anywhere in the output scene.
5. Write `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\report.json` with the schema:
```
{
"kept": ["<node_name>",...], # every node that is now inside "Leftovers"
"deleted": ["<node_name>",...] # every isolated node that was removed
}
```
The two lists must partition the original 20 top-level node names (every input node appears in exactly one list) and `kept` must match the names of the children of the `Leftovers` node in `cleaned.dae`.

Requirements:
1. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\cleaned.dae` parses as valid COLLADA.
2. The output scene has **exactly 1 top-level `<node>`** and it is named `Leftovers`.
3. The `Leftovers` node has at least 2 direct `<node>` children, and that child count matches the size of the single non-singleton connected component recovered from `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\loose.dae` (this is 10 by construction, but the eval recomputes it).
4. Every kept child still references the SAME geometry id it had in `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\loose.dae` (geometry not re-emitted with new ids) and the world-space vertex positions are preserved within 0.1 mm.
5. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\report.json` exists, parses as JSON, has keys `kept` and `deleted`, which together partition the 20 original top-level node names (disjoint union, no duplicates, no extras).
6. The `kept` list equals the set of direct children of `Leftovers` in `cleaned.dae`, and both equal the connectivity-recomputed "connected" set.
7. The `deleted` list equals the connectivity-recomputed "isolated" set and none of those names appear anywhere in `cleaned.dae`.
